memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Balaam answered the donkey, "You have made a fool of me! If only I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now." The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your own donkey, which you have always ridden, to this day? Have I been in the habit of doing this to you?" "No," he said. - Num 22:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam is so blinded by anger that he argues with his own donkey as if this were an everyday thing. He does not marvel that the animal is speaking; he is too consumed by rage to notice the miracle. He even wishes he had a sword to kill it.

The donkey's gentle reasoning exposes Balaam's folly. It reminds him of years of faithful service. Had it ever behaved this way before? No, it had not. The sudden change in the animal's behaviour should have alerted Balaam that something extraordinary was happening. Yet his fury left him blind to the obvious.

Anger does this to us. It narrows our vision until we can see nothing but our own frustration. In the grip of rage, we miss what God is doing, dismiss faithful warnings, and lash out at the very things meant to protect us. A heart on fire with anger is a heart that cannot perceive God's hand.

How much we need the calm and clear-sightedness that comes from walking with the Lord. In Christ we are called to be slow to anger, for human anger does not produce the righteousness God desires (Jas 1:19-20). When you feel rage rising, pause. What is God trying to show you that your anger is hiding?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does anger blind you to what God might be doing?
2. When did anger last cause you to miss something important?
3. What helps you slow down when frustration rises?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, calm the anger that blinds me to Your hand at work. Make me slow to anger and clear-sighted, that I may not miss what You are showing me. Amen.
